title: Bento Guides for Tokens, Buttons, Tables & Charts — Quick Reference and Migration Path
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a compact, scannable set of 'Bento Guides' that live on the docs site and provide: 1) one-page usage patterns for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts; 2) short do/don't pairs for common UX mistakes; 3) quick migration checklist for teams moving from legacy token names and deprecated components; and 4) 16 minimal code examples (React + raw CSS tokens) that can be copied into sandboxes. The goal is to reduce ambiguous implementation questions and reduce internal review iterations on PRs referencing the design system.
acceptance_criteria: Four bento pages (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) published to the docs site under /bento-guides
Each page contains: one-paragraph usage rationale, 3 compact do/don't pairs, 4 concise code examples, and a migration checklist snippet
Searchable titles and metadata so pages surface for queries like 'button accessibility', 'token migration', 'table density patterns'
Design sign-off from Design Lead and documented GH PR with at least two engineering reviews
Metrics tracking: add a doc click counter and a short feedback widget to each page (thumbs + comment)
migration_notes: Token mapping table: provide a left column of legacy tokens (eg. color-500, surface-2) and right column of semantic tokens (eg. bg-default, fg-muted). Include automated codemod link for JS/TS string token replacements.
Buttons: deprecation banner for LegacyButton with instructions: replace <LegacyButton variant="secondary"> with <Button tone="muted" size="md"> and remove custom padding overrides.
Tables: migration notes emphasize switching from table CSS utility classes to Table component props (density, zebra, rowActions) and explain when to keep bespoke table for complex grids.

Charts: recommend using tokenized color palettes and provide mapping from old chart color constants to new theme palettes. Add fallback guidance when custom chart libs bypass tokens (wrap color selection in a token adapter).
examples: Buttons: 4 examples — primary/secondary/ghost/accessibility-contrast; each shows HTML, React and minimal token overrides
Tokens: 4 examples — spacing scale usage, semantic color substitution, responsive token usage, token-based elevation shadows
Tables: 4 examples — dense list, standard data table, table with inline actions, accessibility-focused with keyboard focus ring
Charts: 4 examples — color-safe palette, small-multiples layout, tooltip formatting using tokens, high-contrast mode
do_and_dont: Do: use semantic tokens (bg-default, fg-strong, ui-border) in components so theme swaps are predictable.
Don't: reference legacy numeric color tokens (color-600) directly in feature code — use mapped semantic tokens instead.
Do: prefer props on Table component for density and actions rather than ad hoc CSS overrides.
Don't: increase button hit target by manually bumping padding inside the button; use size tokens and the Button sizing props.
Do: create small code snippets showing desired API usage; keep them copy-paste ready for sandboxes.
Don't: ship new features that require breaking CSS variables without a migration codemod and a clear deprecation window.
